trigger: for a directly-connected (non-gateway) agent, session->stream->Write() returning false is treated as proof of non-delivery by the not_sent release fix; gRPC's C++ streaming contract documents false as terminal call-death, and HTTP/2 framing means a torn-down connection cannot leave a partial CommandRequest frame reassemblable by the peer -- so the feared false-but-delivered outcome has no available mechanism under the actual transport contract
summary: Raised independently by unhappy-path as a SHOULD-severity risk (narrow race, existing gRPC semantics). Re-derived here against the actual send_to() implementation (agent_registry.cpp:647) and gRPC's documented Write() contract plus HTTP/2 framing invariants -- E6 (wrong outcome proven unable to occur) applies at `likely` confidence, capping the band at LOW/NICE rather than the naive I2/HIGH reading. Not verified by fault-injecting a real mid-write connection reset. Documented in ADR-1007's residual-gap section rather than code-fixed -- a real fix (distinguishing definite vs. ambiguous send_to() failure) would change AgentRegistry's contract for dozens of unrelated callers, out of proportion to this round. Advisor-consulted before this disposition was set.
classification_rationale: E6 framing argument caps severity; documented rather than fixed

trigger: for a gateway-routed agent, send_to() returns true the instant the command is queued onto gw_pending_, before the gateway has forwarded it -- so a claim behind a dead/unreachable gateway is never counted as not_sent and depends entirely on the reconciler's TTL
summary: Not a regression introduced by this fix round -- gateway-queued success has never meant confirmed delivery, for this feature or any other dispatch path. But this round's own framing ('releases claims that were taken but never delivered') was accurate only for the direct-agent case; documented explicitly in ADR-1007 so the fix isn't read as closing more than it does. Conservative direction (claim held longer than needed, not released early), so MEDIUM/SHOULD, not a safety gap.
classification_rationale: doc-truth gap about what the fix actually covers, not a code defect

trigger: a per-device InstructionDefinition dispatched via a wired call site (POST /api/instructions/:id/execute, workflow-step dispatch, ScheduleRunner::dispatch_tracked) whose real agent-side execution exceeds the flat 3600s claim TTL before its terminal CommandResponse -- concretely reachable via content_dist.execute_staged (execution-time-unbounded by design) or any ScheduleRunner recurrence shorter than a legitimately-slow per-device definition's real duration (e.g. an hourly vuln_scan.scan taking 90 minutes)
summary: The reconciler force-releases any claim past its flat one-hour expires_at with no way to distinguish a crashed agent from one still legitimately executing -- since no production caller populates the wire command's expires_at (dead code, per the ADR's own admission), every claim used the same flat default, so any per-device command genuinely running longer than an hour got its still-in-use claim force-released, admitting a real concurrent second dispatch -- the exact failure this feature exists to prevent. No fault injection required; an ordinary long-running command on a tight schedule reproduces it deterministically. FIXED: ExecutionTracker::renew_concurrency_claim extends expires_at by another full TTL window on every non-terminal ('running') progress response, so the reconciler's TTL now measures time since the agent's LAST progress signal, not time since the claim was first taken. Regression test: test_execution_tracker.cpp, "a 'running' status renews the claim's expires_at...(CHAOS-TTL-1)".
classification_rationale: code force-released a claim for work known (via its own progress signal) to still be in flight, contradicting the feature's stated purpose

recorded_by: claude (this session, external-model adjudication via codex/gpt-5.6-sol opine)
trigger: a MUTATING per-device InstructionDefinition whose real agent-side execution exceeds the flat 3600s claim TTL without crossing the agent's 64KB output-auto-flush threshold (the ONLY path that emits a mid-run 'running' CommandResponse today, per CommandContextImpl::flush_output_locked in agent.cpp) before its terminal CommandResponse. Verified concrete trigger: device.script_exec.* (content/definitions/script_exec.yaml, concurrency: per-device) accepts an operator-configured timeout up to 3600s and is mutating (runs an operator-named program or authored script that can hold real state); a quiet script producing little stdout can legitimately run to that ceiling with zero wire traffic to renew its claim.
summary: SUPERSEDES this finding's pass_ordinal:3 row, which was marked 'fixed' in error. The renewal fix committed in 6edbc2baa (ExecutionTracker::renew_concurrency_claim, wired from update_agent_status on 'running' responses) is real, correct, tested server-side plumbing, but self-verification against the agent-side plugin code AFTER committing found it does not reach either of that row's own named triggers -- vuln_scan's ctx.report_progress() is a local no-op with zero wire traffic, and (correction, per external-model review) content_dist.execute_staged is NOT unbounded as originally claimed (it has a real 30-minute deadline, content_dist_exec_parsers.hpp) so it cannot actually reach the 3600s TTL and is not a valid trigger for this finding. An external-model second opinion (gpt-5.6-sol via /codex opine) identified device.script_exec.* as a corrected, verified, MUTATING trigger: per-device, an operator-settable timeout up to 3600s, and no output-callback wiring guarantee of crossing the 64KB auto-flush threshold within that window. Because the affected instruction class is MUTATING (a script/program that can hold real state, e.g. a partially-written file or in-flight package operation), a duplicate concurrent execution can repeat a non-idempotent state mutation -- this derives IMPACT=I2 (data/state corruption), which alone gives HIGH regardless of the 'false assurance' I6 raise this row's predecessor relied on. Re-opened to 'open' rather than superseded to a lower severity.
classification_rationale: code force-releases a claim for mutating work that may still be in flight, contradicting the feature's stated purpose; the prior row's 'fixed' disposition was itself a self-authored claim not independently verified before recording

trigger: a MUTATING per-device InstructionDefinition whose real agent-side execution exceeds the flat 3600s claim TTL without crossing the agent's 64KB output-auto-flush threshold; verified concrete trigger device.script_exec.* (operator-configurable timeout up to 3600s)
summary: SUPERSEDES pass_ordinal:4 (open). Fixed with a plugin-cooperation-independent agent-core keepalive: a per-connection background thread (agents/core/src/agent.cpp, spawned/torn-down mirroring the existing heartbeat thread's lifecycle) sends a periodic bare RUNNING (output sentinel '__keepalive__') for every command in in_flight_ids_ -- a set populated the instant a command is accepted onto the bounded dispatch queue (covers queue-wait time, not just execute()) and erased at the single record_command_terminal chokepoint every terminal write already passes through, on all exit paths including queue-full rejection. The server recognizes the sentinel on both the direct-Subscribe (process_agent_response) and gateway-streamed (process_gateway_response) RUNNING paths in agent_service_impl.cpp and routes it to notify_exec_tracker (triggering ExecutionTracker::renew_concurrency_claim from pass_ordinal:3/UP-1's fix), without storing a ResponseStore row, publishing an SSE output line, or counting an analytics event -- matching the existing __timing__ frame's own intercept pattern. Tested: full agent + server suites green (agent 2/2, server 21/21 test cases, 1789+ assertions), a new dedicated regression test in test_agent_service_impl.cpp proves the sentinel reaches ExecutionTracker via notify_exec_tracker AND is excluded from ResponseStore in the same assertion. ADR-1007 corrected to CLOSED with the full mechanism description.
classification_rationale: was: code force-released a claim for mutating work that may still be in flight; now: fixed with a signal independent of the code path that made the original finding true

trigger: an ordinary command completes while the agent-core keepalive thread's periodic snapshot-then-write sweep is mid-iteration for that same command -- no attacker required, pure timing artifact of legitimate concurrent operation
summary: A stale __keepalive__ RUNNING response arriving strictly after a command's real terminal response could unconditionally flip an already-terminal agent_exec_status row back to status='running', completed_at=0, with no self-healing signal ever arriving afterward (agents do not re-send a terminal status) -- corrupting the executions drawer / SSE / per-agent KPI surface. Found by a targeted security-guardian re-review of the CHAOS-TTL-1 keepalive fix (pass_ordinal 5), which this session requested BEFORE finalizing given the substantial new agent-core code added. The per-device concurrency CLAIM itself was never at risk (release_concurrency_claim's WHERE released_at IS NULL prevents a stale write from resurrecting an already-released claim) -- this is a data-integrity finding on the tracking/observability surface, not a re-opening of CHAOS-TTL-1's original dispatch-safety guarantee.
classification_rationale: unconditional upsert let a stale non-terminal write overwrite a terminal one, with no ordering guard
waiver_rationale: Fixed: ExecutionTracker::upsert_agent_status_once's ON CONFLICT upsert now makes terminal status STICKY via a CASE guard on every column (status/completed_at/exit_code/error_detail/plugin_result_status) -- once a row is in the terminal set, a 'running' write is a no-op on all of them. The SSE agent-transition payload was also fixed to use RETURNING (the actual post-write row) instead of the caller-supplied `s` verbatim, so a correctly-rejected stale write no longer publishes a misleading 'running' event either. Regression test: test_execution_tracker.cpp 'a stale running update arriving AFTER a terminal status does not regress the row (CHAOS-TTL-1 keepalive hardening)', which also proves a genuine second terminal write (HA WS-0 redelivery) still applies normally.

trigger: an exception escaping the per-connection Subscribe read-loop scope in agents/core/src/agent.cpp between the keepalive-thread spawn and the manual per-connection teardown -- this file's own thread_pool_ re-creation try/catch a few lines up exists BECAUSE this exact region has thrown in production under host resource exhaustion, so this is not a hypothetical trigger
policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect of the kind cpp-safety blocks (use-after-free / borrowed-data escape) -- CLAUDE.md policy floor, gates regardless of derived band
summary: The manual per-connection teardown (stop+join keepalive_thread_) is plain sequential code, not itself exception-safe. An exception unwinding past it goes straight to `sub_slot`'s ~CtxSlot (which only retracts subscribe_ctx_ to null, never cancels) and then destroys the stack-local `sub_ctx` -- while keepalive_thread_ may still be inside or about to enter stream->Write(), which depends on that ClientContext through gRPC's internal reference. A genuine use-after-free / borrowed-data-escape hazard, found by a targeted cpp-safety re-review of the CHAOS-TTL-1 keepalive fix requested before finalizing given the substantial new thread/lifecycle code added.
classification_rationale: new thread added to an already-fragile exception-escape window without the same protection its own design intent (exact mirror of heartbeat_thread_) implied it should have
waiver_rationale: Fixed with a scope-order RAII guard (ScopeExit keepalive_unwind_guard) declared AFTER stream/sub_slot/sub_ctx, so C++'s reverse-destruction-order guarantee makes it the FIRST thing to run on unwind -- stopping and joining keepalive_thread_ before sub_slot/sub_ctx can destruct, on every exit path including an exception. A no-op on the ordinary path (the manual teardown already joined it by then). Also corrected two doc comments that incorrectly claimed stream->Write() 'never blocks' (contradicted by stop()'s own documented guardian_sink_stream_ blocking-Write hazard) -- the real reasoning is that both existing join sites are reached only after stream->Read() has already returned false, proving the connection dead rather than merely stalled.
